'''Kaizu-hime no Mikoto''' (会津比売命 / あいづひめのみこと) is a deity associated with folk traditions in [[Nagano Prefecture]], particularly in the Suwa region. She is venerated as a divine figure in the [[Suwa Shrine|Suwa Faith]].
== Overview ==
The [[Kaizu-hime Shrine|Aizuhime Shrine]] (会津比売神社) venerates her as '''Kaizu-hime no Kami''' (会津比売神).
The origin of the name "Kaizu" is unclear, though it may derive from the historical name of the surrounding Matsushiro (松代町) area, which was traditionally called "Kaizu" (海津). [[Matsushiro Castle]] was also historically known as Kaizu Castle.
According to the [[Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku]], she was enshrined as Aitsuhime no Kami (會津比賣神) and received the Rank of Junior Fourth Rank (従四位) in 866 CE.<ref>諏訪史料叢書 巻28, p. 73</ref>
Traditions associate her as the wife of Takeiwanese no Mikoto (武五百建命), the first [[Shinano Province]] governor and probable occupant of the [[Hanishina Kofun group|Mori Shogun-zuka Kofun]]. She is sometimes identified with Itsuhaya-hime no Mikoto (伊津速比売神), another deity linked to [[Takeminakata]]'s lineage.
A legend claims that her tomb lies atop Tsumaonna Mountain (妻女山), and the mountain's name is said to originate from her story.
== Genealogy ==
At [[Kaizu-hime Shrine|Aizuhime Shrine]], she is considered the daughter of Izuhayao-no-Mikoto (伊豆速雄命), a child of [[Takeminakata]]. Other sources suggest that she was the daughter of Yatsugata no Sukune no Kami (八縣宿禰神) (also known as Rokuo Hiko no Kami), with siblings such as Kamoha no Kami (可毛羽神) and Kusanoi-hime (草奈井比売神).<ref>"諏訪下社大祝武居祝系圖略," 諏訪史料叢書 巻28, 諏訪教育会, 昭和11th year , p. 73</ref>
